narrative.summary: On a chilly autumn evening aboard a transatlantic ocean liner, Neville Fairweather is found stabbed to death. Witnesses insist they saw Neville alive and strolling on the exclusive first-class promenade deck at twenty minutes past eight at night. However, a closer look reveals that the figure was an impersonation by a crew member, exploiting social and class segregation to conceal the real time of death. Katherine Bellamy, an astute passenger, pieces together evidence of mistaken identity, restricted access, and crew schedules to expose the truth and identify the killer.

accepted_facts: Neville Fairweather was stabbed with a dagger to the heart.
Witnesses saw a man resembling Neville on the first-class promenade deck at twenty minutes past eight at night.
Crew logbook records the deck steward leaving crew quarters at ten minutes past eight at night.
A torn edge of uniform fabric was found snagged on Neville's cabin doorframe.
The murder weapon dagger was kept in the ship's secure armory, under control of Dr. Cecil Ashgrove.
Ferdinand Carrick had no alibi for the time of the actual murder.
inferred_conclusions: The figure seen on the promenade deck was an impersonation by Iris Selwyn, the deck steward.
Neville Fairweather was actually killed at ten minutes past eight at night, before the promenade sighting.
Ferdinand Carrick exploited the impersonation to create an alibi and commit the murder.
The torn uniform fabric proves the deck steward impersonated Neville to mislead witnesses.

mechanism.description: The murderer exploited the strict class segregation and crew uniform to impersonate Neville Fairweather. Iris Selwyn, the deck steward, dressed in a similar uniform and mimicked Neville's mannerisms on the first-class promenade deck at twenty minutes past eight, creating a false sighting. Meanwhile, the real Neville was stabbed to death at ten minutes past eight. The key physical clue is a torn edge of the steward's uniform fabric snagged on Neville's cabin doorframe, inconsistent with Neville's usual clothes. Crew logs confirm the steward left the crew quarters at ten minutes past eight, enabling the impersonation. The murder weapon was taken from the ship's armory, accessible to Ferdinand Carrick and Dr. Ashgrove, but only Carrick had motive and opportunity. By exploiting witness expectations and social constraints, the culprit concealed the real time and identity of the victim, gaining an alibi.

delivery_path.step: The torn fabric found on the victim's cabin doorframe was identified as steward uniform material.
Crew logbook shows Iris Selwyn, the deck steward, left crew quarters at ten minutes past eight.

false_assumption.statement: The man seen on the first-class promenade deck at twenty minutes past eight was Neville Fairweather himself, alive and well.
false_assumption.why_it_seems_reasonable: Witnesses recognized the figure by his customary attire, stature, and mannerisms, and had no reason to suspect an impersonation, especially given class segregation limiting access to the first-class decks.
false_assumption.what_it_hides: It conceals the real time of death at ten minutes past eight and the identity of the impersonator (Iris Selwyn), allowing the killer to establish a false alibi.

red_herrings.innocent_explanation: Carrick was anxious about a business deal unrelated to the murder and had no confirmed access to the victim at the murder time.

closed_circle.rationale: All suspects were aboard the ship during the murder window with no external access possible. The victim and crew schedules restrict possible killers to this group.

discriminating_test.design: A reenactment is staged where Iris Selwyn wears her steward uniform and mimics Neville Fairweather's mannerisms on the first-class promenade deck at the historically logged time. Simultaneously, crew logbooks, uniform fabric comparisons, and witness statements are cross-examined to prove the imposture and expose Ferdinand Carrick as the only suspect who had motive, access to the dagger, and no alibi for the actual time of death.
discriminating_test.knowledge_revealed: The test reveals the impersonation of Neville Fairweather by Iris Selwyn, the true time of death at ten minutes past eight, and Ferdinand Carrick's guilt through his disturbance of the murder weapon and lack of alibi.
discriminating_test.pass_condition: If witnesses confirm the impersonation reenactment and the physical fabric evidence matches the steward's uniform, while Ferdinand Carrick cannot provide a valid alibi for the actual murder time, he is proven guilty.

fair_play.explanation: Step 1: The glove smudge on the dagger and armory inspection logs (early) eliminate Lavinia Yardley. Step 2: Crew logbooks and torn uniform fabric (mid) identify Iris Selwyn as impersonator. Step 3: Handling marks on dagger and armory access (mid) narrow suspects to Ferdinand Carrick and Dr. Ashgrove. Step 4: Timing contradictions in steward log and witness sighting (mid) expose the false alibi and real murder time, implicating Ferdinand Carrick. All clues appear before the discriminating test, enabling the reader to logically deduce the culprit.
